title: Choose Cloudly's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Cloud Atlas. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Cloud Atlas Station
options.lineage: 1896 International Cloud Atlas chromolithographs + WMO station-model notation
options.thesis: Your VM is your observing station; every run is a classified, logged observation, with spend read off a barometer.
options.viewport: A cobalt field holding Plate I: a live WebGL cumulus that grows course by course as a real run replays beside it, ending in a PR; the install command sits on a chalk card with an international-orange copy button.
options.risk: A cloud brand drawing clouds can read as cute; meteorology must stay the second layer under plain labels ($1.42, Running), and the volumetric cloud needs a static plate fallback on weak GPUs.

raised.raise: The run log is banded in strict horizontal courses, one event per course, a record built upward instead of a chat scroll.
The page descends through the atlas's three altitude tiers (high, middle, low cloud) on real depth planes, landing on your station at ground level.
The task composer and the run record are one object: the observation form you fill in becomes the logged observation.
Run states resolve hard, with no in-between tints; finished runs are inked closed.
International orange (the windsock colour) appears only on what can be pressed.

options.label: The Breaker Panel
options.lineage: residential electrical service panels and utility meters
options.thesis: Each harness is a labeled breaker you flip on; the spend limit is the main breaker, and it really trips.
options.viewport: A 3D panel door swings open on a row of breakers labeled Claude Code, Codex, Gemini; flipping one starts a replayed run, and the main breaker trips at the limit.
options.risk: The most mechanically literal reading of the spend limit; steel-and-toggle skeuomorphism can feel heavy on the dense app screens.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Runs as departures: rows flip from Queued to Running to PR opened, character by character.
options.viewport: A live board of runs (repo, harness, status, spend) cascading as a replay plays, with the install line as the next departure.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and developers identify with status boards; it holds audience identification but explains own-your-VM and the spend limit less clearly than the atlas.
options.risk: A familiar dev-tool motif and the darkest card here, which edges toward the terminal look you ruled out.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: Runs as courses coiled upward into a tower.
options.viewport: A tower rising one course per run event.
options.case: Fuses poorly: developers who self-host don't identify with clay work, and it explains none of the mechanism.
options.risk: Pure metaphor with no product facts behind it.
options.kept: Strict horizontal banding: one event per course.

options.label: Multiplane Cel Dawn
options.thesis: Painted planes slide past as the camera sinks toward a lit cottage.
options.viewport: Parallax forest sinking toward a lamp.
options.case: Fuses weakly: lovely depth, but storybook warmth undercuts a tool about money and code.
options.risk: Reads as a film title sequence, not a product.
options.kept: Real depth planes traveled on scroll.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: One-bit cards where reading and making are one mode.
options.viewport: A card stack for tasks and runs.
options.case: Fuses weakly: nostalgic for some developers, but it can't show runs, spend or where things run.
options.risk: Retro novelty with no colour to signal state.
options.kept: The form you fill in is the record it creates.

options.label: Weimar Cabaret Bill
options.thesis: Acid yellow on black, the programme leaning off vertical.
options.case: Fuses poorly: theatrical where the audience wants plain cost and control.
options.kept: Hard two-state run states; finished runs struck through.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, one action colour, friendly labels.
options.viewport: A single column of friendly cards.
options.case: Fuses blandly: clear, but it's the generic look you asked to avoid.
options.kept: One action colour, reserved for what can be pressed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer-tool landing page, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and install command on the left, an app screenshot on the right, features underneath.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other agent tool by design.
